exercise.name: Alternate Heel Touch Side Kick Squat
aliases: Squat heel touch with side kick
Squat to side kick with heel tap

reference.title: Alternate Heel Touch Side Kick Squat
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be read at authoring time because the proxy blocked it, so the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (squat with a reach, then a single-leg hip abduction)

breathing.pattern: Inhale as you squat and reach, exhale as you stand and kick.

prescription.tempo: Controlled squat, quick but controlled kick
prescription.frequency: 2-3 times a week or as a conditioning circuit
prescription.progression: Higher kick, pause in the kick, then a faster pace

cues.text: Feet about hip width, hands together in front of the chest.
Squat and reach the right hand down the outside of the right leg to touch the right heel; left arm reaches forward.
Touch lightly; heels stay down, back long.
Stand up, hands back to the chest.
Shift onto the left leg and kick the straight right leg out to the side, foot flexed.
Lower it under control beside the left foot.
Repeat to the left: touch the left heel, kick the left leg.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding hard through the back to reach the heel
mistakes.fix: Squat deeper and bend sideways; touch the ankle if the heel is too far.
Sit the hips back and keep the weight over the mid-foot.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning far over the standing leg to lift the kick higher
mistakes.fix: Kick only as high as you can with a small trunk lean.

mistakes.mistake: Kicking forward instead of to the side
mistakes.fix: Lead with the heel straight out to the side, toes facing forward.

kinematics.peak: Back to the same spot after each kick
≈102° R / ≈102° L at the heel touch
kinematics.norm: Deep enough for the hand to reach the heel, about 100-120 degrees (clinical opinion); depth is driven mostly by knee range of motion (Zawadka 2020)

kinematics.peak: Trunk ≈50° forward, side-bent ≈24° to the right; right fingertips 8 cm from the outside of the right heel (rig hand tip)
kinematics.norm: Hand reaches the outside of the same-side heel with a forward lean and a side bend (reference movement; clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: Right leg ≈50° out from vertical (hip abduction ≈42°), foot 39 cm up; trunk leaning ≈10° away
kinematics.norm: Standing hip abduction is a common gluteus medius exercise; side-lying abduction gave high gluteus medius activity (Boren 2011, Selkowitz 2013). About 30-45 degrees of abduction is typical (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: Per side 1 s down, 0.3 s touch, 0.8 s up, 0.5 s kick, 0.6 s back
kinematics.norm: Controlled, about 4 s per side (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual 7630, Alternate Heel Touch Side Kick Squat, video (movement reference)
Zawadka et al. 2020, How are squat timing and kinematics in the sagittal plane related to squat depth? (J Sports Sci Med 19:500-507)
Boren et al. 2011, EMG analysis of gluteus medius and gluteus maximus during rehabilitation exercises (Int J Sports Phys Ther 6(3):206-223; PMC3201064)

Selkowitz, Beneck & Powers 2013, which exercises target the gluteal muscles while minimizing activation of the tensor fascia lata? Fine-wire EMG of 11 exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 43(2):54-64)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Clear the space beside you before kicking.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Balance concerns: one hand on a wall or chair for the kick.
Tight hamstrings or back: touch the ankle or shin instead of the heel.
regressions: Bodyweight squat, then standing side leg raise.
progressions: Mini band above the knees (when available).

muscleNotes.quads_r: Control the squat and drive the stand; the standing leg holds a soft knee in the kick (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Control the squat and drive the stand; the standing leg holds a soft knee in the kick (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Hip extensor for the stand out of the squat (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Hip extensor for the stand out of the squat (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Kicks the leg out to the side and steadies the pelvis over the standing leg; side-lying abduction gave high gluteus medius activity (Boren 2011; Selkowitz 2013).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Kicks the leg out to the side and steadies the pelvis over the standing leg; side-lying abduction gave high gluteus medius activity (Boren 2011; Selkowitz 2013).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Help extend the hips in the squat and control the kick back down (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Help extend the hips in the squat and control the kick back down (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Hip extensors with the glutes; lengthen as the trunk leans to reach the heel (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Hip extensors with the glutes; lengthen as the trunk leans to reach the heel (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Side-bend the trunk toward the heel and hold it level in the kick (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Side-bend the trunk toward the heel and hold it level in the kick (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Keep the kicking leg from drifting back (tensor fasciae latae and gluteus minimus help abduct; Selkowitz 2013).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Keep the kicking leg from drifting back (tensor fasciae latae and gluteus minimus help abduct; Selkowitz 2013).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk steady through the reach and on one leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold a long back in the forward lean (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold a long back in the forward lean (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.calves_r: Balance on the standing foot (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.calves_l: Balance on the standing foot (clinical opinion).
